Dayton

the Gem City — birthplace of aviation on the Great Miami

74 places · 55 sights · 19 to eat & drink · 7 areas · 35 sources · status last checked 2026-08-24

Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station 26

  1. Must see · Dayton-Style Pizza · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Wheat Penny Oven and Bar

    Chef Elizabeth Wiley's Oregon District spot (since 2013) for creative deck-oven pizzas (the Bright Eyes with zucchini and lemon), pastas and eggplant fries, with plenty of gluten-free and vegetarian options.

    515 Wayne Ave, Dayton, OH 45410

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Dayton Local, GIRLABOUTDAYTON

  2. Must see · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Dayton Art Institute

    1930 Italian-Renaissance-villa art museum overlooking downtown, with 20,000+ works across 5,000 years; anchors the Grafton Hill bluff. Open Wed-Sun.

    456 Belmonte Park N, Dayton, OH 45405

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  3. Must see · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Oregon District

    Dayton's oldest neighborhood and nightlife heart: a quarter-mile of brick-lined East Fifth Street lined with bars, restaurants and shops, named an APA Great Street. Best-preserved 1820-1915 architecture in the city.

    E Fifth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

  4. Must see · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    2nd Street Market

    Five Rivers MetroParks' year-round public market in a restored railroad freight house downtown; 50+ local growers, makers and prepared-food vendors. Free admission and parking, open Fri-Sun.

    600 E 2nd St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Dayton Local

  5. Must see · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Victoria Theatre

    One of the oldest continually operating theaters on the continent, opened 1866 as the Turner Opera House; a restored 1,154-seat National Register venue for Broadway tours, concerts and film.

    138 N Main St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  6. Must see · Ice Cream, Candy & Bakeries · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Esther Price Candies

    Dayton's beloved chocolatier since 1926; every piece is still made by hand at the Wayne Avenue factory built around Esther's own house. The caramel creams and assorted boxes are the classics.

    1709 Wayne Ave, Dayton, OH 45410

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Local

  7. Must see · American & New American · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    The Pine Club

    Cash-friendly Dayton supper club since 1947, no reservations, pine-paneled and unchanged; the NY Times called it one of the world's 10 greatest traditional dining rooms. Steaks come with the legendary stewed tomatoes.

    1926 Brown St, Dayton, OH 45409

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  8. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    The Century Bar

    Dayton's bourbon house since 1942: 800+ whiskeys, single-barrel pours and craft cocktails at an Edwardian hand-carved wood bar. Consistently rated among the nation's best whiskey bars.

    18 S Jefferson St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  9. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    The Trolley Stop

    Dayton's oldest continuously operating tavern, in an 1839 Oregon District building; a patio, live music and pub plates. The history is the draw as much as the beer.

    530 E Fifth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Dayton Local

  10. Must see · Mexican & Latin · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Salar Restaurant and Lounge

    Upscale-casual Oregon District kitchen of world-fusion cuisine with strong Peruvian roots — ceviche, lomo saltado — plus two patios and full bars looking onto Fifth Street.

    400 E Fifth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Local, Official site / operator

  11. Must see · American & New American · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Lily's Bistro

    Chef-owner Emily Mendenhall's Oregon District bistro (since 2013) with daily-changing seasonal menus blending American Southern and tropical flavors, plus a tiki-inspired cocktail program.

    329 E Fifth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, WHIO / WDTN (TV news)

  12. Must see · Mediterranean & Middle Eastern · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Coco's Bistro

    Longtime South-of-downtown bistro with a lush, eclectic dining room serving Mediterranean-leaning New American plates; a Dayton date-night standby.

    250 Warren St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Local, Official site / operator

  13. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Warped Wing Brewing Company

    Dayton's flagship craft brewery (since 2014) in a downtown former foundry; Best of Dayton brewery winner. Ermal's Cream Ale honors the local inventor of the pull-tab can.

    26 Wyandot St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Dayton Local

  14. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Tender Mercy

    Award-winning underground speakeasy hidden in the lower level of the Avant-Garde Building; its back room houses Dozo, a chef-driven omakase-style sushi 'permanent pop-up' (head chef Yudi Alviando). A viral social pick — Kait Lott's 'Don't Sleep on Dayton' hidden-bar video.

    607 E 3rd St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by KAITS, Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

  15. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Dayton Arcade

    1904 Flemish-façade glass-domed arcade, a downtown landmark reborn after a $162M restoration wrapped in 2025 (Hilton Garden Inn, food hall, shops); the rotunda dome is the showpiece.

    35 W Fourth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Official site / operator, DAYTONVISTAS

  16. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Boonshoft Museum of Discovery

    Hands-on science-and-nature museum with a planetarium, small zoo and children's exhibits north of downtown; the region's top family science destination.

    2600 Deweese Pkwy, Dayton, OH 45414

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  17. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    RiverScape MetroPark

    Downtown riverfront park at the Great Miami confluence: Five Rivers Fountain of Lights, splash pad, winter ice rink, kayak and bike rentals, and the hub of the region's paved trail network. Free.

    111 E Monument Ave, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  18. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Woodland Cemetery & Arboretum

    1841 garden cemetery and 200-acre arboretum on rolling hills; resting place of the Wright brothers, Paul Laurence Dunbar, Erma Bombeck and Charles Kettering, with a Tiffany-windowed Romanesque chapel. Free.

    118 Woodland Ave, Dayton, OH 45409

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  19. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    America's Packard Museum

    World's largest collection of Packard automobiles and memorabilia, displayed inside a beautifully restored original 1917 Packard dealership showroom downtown.

    420 S Ludlow St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  20. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Day Air Ballpark (Dayton Dragons)

    Downtown home of the Dayton Dragons, holders of pro sports' longest consecutive sellout streak (1,600+ games); a beloved summer-evening institution on Monument Avenue.

    220 N Patterson Blvd, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

  21. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Benjamin & Marian Schuster Performing Arts Center

    Dayton's flagship performing-arts center (opened 2003), home to the Dayton Philharmonic, Opera and Ballet under a fiber-optic 'Wintergarden' star ceiling.

    1 W 2nd St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Local

  22. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Island MetroPark

    Riverfront MetroPark at the confluence of the Stillwater and Great Miami rivers, with a rowing boathouse, playground and a red bridge linking the Great Miami and Stillwater river trails.

    101 E Helena St, Dayton, OH 45404

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Dayton Local

  23. Worth the detour · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Deeds Point MetroPark

    Small riverside MetroPark at the confluence of the Mad and Great Miami rivers offering the best unobstructed view of the downtown Dayton skyline and RiverScape fountains.

    510 Webster St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Official site / operator, DESTDAYTON

  24. Worth the detour · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Lucky's Taproom & Eatery

    Oregon District taproom (since 2011) with a rotating craft-beer list, pub fare and one of the city's most extensive vegan menus. Reliable pre- or post-show spot on Fifth.

    520 E Fifth St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Local, Official site / operator

  25. Worth the detour · Breweries & Bars · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Fifth Street Brewpub

    One of the nation's only co-op-owned brewpubs (3,000+ member-owners) in a St. Anne's Hill building serving food and drink since 1856; scratch pub fare a short walk from the Oregon District.

    1600 E 5th St, Dayton, OH 45403

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Ohio Magazine

  26. Deep cut · Downtown, Oregon District & Webster Station

    Old Court House

    1850 Greek Revival courthouse modeled on the Temple of Hephaestus, on whose steps Lincoln gave an 1859 anti-slavery speech; now the Montgomery County Historical Society museum in Courthouse Square. Free.

    7 N Main St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton 6

  1. Must see · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    Possum Creek MetroPark

    West Dayton MetroPark with a working educational farm, fishing at Argonne Lake and trails through the former Argonne Forest amusement park grounds.

    4790 Frytown Rd, Dayton, OH 45417

    Recommended by Official site / operator, DESTDAYTON

  2. Must see · Soul, BBQ & Southern · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    Mz. Jade's Soul Food

    Popular soul-food kitchen inside West Social Tap & Table in the historic Wright-Dunbar district: oxtails, fried chicken, candied yams, mac & cheese and collard greens.

    1100 W Third St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, WHIO / WDTN (TV news)

  3. Must see · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    Wright Cycle Company

    NPS-run bike shop where the Wright brothers designed and built the machines that led to the 1903 first flight; the anchor of Dayton Aviation Heritage NHP in the Wright-Dunbar district. Free.

    16 S Williams St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by NATIONAL PARK SVC, NATIONAL PARK SVC

  4. Worth the detour · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    SunWatch Indian Village

    Reconstructed Fort Ancient (c. 1200 CE) Native American village and solar-calendar site on the Great Miami River, a National Historic Landmark now operated by Boonshoft; open seasonally.

    2301 W River Rd, Dayton, OH 45418

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  5. Worth the detour · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    Paul Laurence Dunbar House Historic Site

    1904-06 home of pioneering Black poet Paul Laurence Dunbar, preserved with his belongings; Ohio's first state memorial to an African American (1936) and part of the aviation-heritage park.

    219 Paul Laurence Dunbar St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by Ohio History Connection, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  6. Worth the detour · Wright-Dunbar & West Dayton

    Wright-Dunbar Interpretive Center

    NPS visitor center in the Wrights' former print-shop building; tells the intertwined stories of Wilbur, Orville and their classmate, poet Paul Laurence Dunbar. Free, gateway to the Wright-Dunbar aviation trail.

    16 S Williams St, Dayton, OH 45402

    Recommended by NATIONAL PARK SVC, NATIONAL PARK SVC

Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville 9

  1. Must see · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Carillon Historical Park

    65-acre Dayton History campus built around the original 1905 Wright Flyer III, the only airplane that is a National Historic Landmark, gifted by Orville Wright himself and shown in a purpose-built pit.

    1000 Carillon Blvd, Dayton, OH 45409

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  2. Must see · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Fraze Pavilion

    Intimate 4,300-seat outdoor amphitheater (opened 1991) in Kettering's Lincoln Park Civic Commons, named for pop-top inventor Ermal Fraze; a summer calendar of national concerts, comedy and free festivals.

    695 Lincoln Park Blvd, Kettering, OH 45429

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  3. Must see · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Sugarcreek MetroPark

    Rolling MetroPark in Bellbrook famous for the Osage Orange Tunnel (an 1880s fence-row grown into an arching green corridor) and the Three Sisters, a trio of oaks dating to the 1440s.

    4178 Conference Rd, Bellbrook, OH 45305

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Official site / operator

  4. Must see · Ice Cream, Candy & Bakeries · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Bill's Donut Shop

    A 24/7 Centerville institution since 1979, named to national 'best donut' lists (People, USA Today) and a perennial Best of Dayton winner. The airy glazed yeast donut is the one to get.

    268 N Main St, Centerville, OH 45459

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, WHIO / WDTN (TV news)

  5. Must see · Mexican & Latin · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    El Meson

    Family-run (Castro family) West Carrollton mainstay of 45+ years serving Spanish and Latin American tapas, paella and a deep wine list; a Dayton special-occasion favorite.

    903 E Dixie Dr, West Carrollton, OH 45449

    Recommended by Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com, Dayton Local

  6. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Carillon Brewing Co.

    The nation's only production brewery inside a museum: costumed brewers make beer to mid-19th-century Dayton recipes on replica equipment at Carillon Park, paired with historic immigrant fare.

    1000 Carillon Blvd, Dayton, OH 45409

    Recommended by The Dayton Magazine, Official site / operator

  7. Worth the detour · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Hawthorn Hill

    Orville Wright's grand 1914 Oakwood mansion (a National Historic Landmark) where he lived until his death; toured by advance-reservation shuttle from Carillon Park on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

    901 Harman Ave, Oakwood, OH 45419

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

  8. Worth the detour · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Cox Arboretum MetroPark

    189-acre MetroPark of formal gardens, a butterfly house, edible-landscape and towering observation tower south of the city. Open daily, free.

    6733 Springboro Pike, Dayton, OH 45449

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  9. Worth the detour · Kettering, Oakwood & Centerville

    Hills & Dales MetroPark

    Wooded Kettering MetroPark laid out with input from the Olmsted firm; ridge and valley hiking trails, stone shelters and the historic Dogwood Pond.

    2655 S Patterson Blvd, Kettering, OH 45409

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Dayton Local

Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy 6

  1. Must see · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Rose Music Center at The Heights

    4,200-seat fully covered outdoor amphitheater in Huber Heights (opened 2015), the north suburbs' marquee live-music venue — a full season of national touring acts under a weatherproof shelter, with lawn, terrace and box seating.

    Look for amphitheater concerts

    6800 Executive Blvd, Huber Heights, OH 45424

    Recommended by DESTDAYTON, Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  2. Must see · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Englewood MetroPark

    1,900-acre MetroPark around the Stillwater River and Englewood dam, home to three waterfalls (Martindale, Patty and Oaks) reached along the 3.8-mile Green Trail.

    100 E National Rd, Englewood, OH 45322

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  3. Must see · Dayton-Style Pizza · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Marion's Piazza

    The originator of Dayton-style pizza (est. 1965): a cracker-thin crust cut into small squares, sold by the million each year. This N. Dixie location is a longtime local flagship.

    3443 N Dixie Dr, Dayton, OH 45414

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Local

  4. Worth the detour · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Wegerzyn Gardens MetroPark

    88-acre MetroPark along the Stillwater River with formal English, Federal and Victorian gardens, a Children's Discovery Garden and woodland boardwalk.

    1301 E Siebenthaler Ave, Dayton, OH 45414

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Dayton Local

  5. Worth the detour · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Taylorsville MetroPark

    Five Rivers MetroPark on the site of vanished canal town Tadmor: 8+ miles of trail with real elevation, old-growth forest and Great Miami River overlooks, remnants of the 1845 Miami-Erie Canal, and a stretch of the Buckeye and North Country national trails. Free.

    Look for Tadmor canal trails overlook

    2000 US-40, Vandalia, OH 45377

    Recommended by Five Rivers MetroParks (official), Miami Conservancy District

  6. Worth the detour · Vandalia, Huber Heights & Troy

    Troy Historic Public Square

    The heart of Troy: a traffic-circle square with a lively fountain and gardens, ringed by Victorian storefronts, shops and restaurants — the whole square is on the National Register of Historic Places. The fountain runs red each June for the Strawberry Festival.

    Look for fountain Victorian square

    Public Square, Troy, OH 45373

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Home Grown Great / Miami County VCB

Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson 10

  1. Must see · Asian · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Wat Da Pho

    The Dayton area's best-known and best-rated pho house — a family-owned Beavercreek kitchen keeping its broth close to the family's Vietnamese recipe. Google 4.7 across ~2,000 reviews; Dayton937's "Quest for the Best Pho" ranks it the region's top bowl.

    3464 Pentagon Blvd Ste D, Beavercreek, OH 45431

    Recommended by DAYTON937, Dayton Local, Official site / operator

  2. Must see · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    National Museum of the U.S. Air Force

    The marquee: world's largest and oldest military aviation museum, 4 hangars of aircraft from the Wright 1909 Military Flyer to an SR-71, XB-70 and presidential planes. Free admission, free parking, open daily 9-5.

    1100 Spaatz St, Wright-Patterson AFB, OH 45433

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  3. Must see · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Eastwood MetroPark

    437-acre MetroPark on the Mad River with a 185-acre lake for boating, sailing, fishing and paddling, plus ponds, trails and prime birdwatching.

    1385 Harshman Rd, Dayton, OH 45431

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  4. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Huffman Prairie Flying Field

    The 84-acre pasture where the Wrights perfected controlled, powered flight in 1904-05 and ran the world's first flying school. NPS site on WPAFB, free, with an interpretive center at the Wright Memorial.

    2380 Memorial Rd, Wright-Patterson AFB, OH 45433

    Recommended by NATIONAL PARK SVC, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  5. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Narrows Reserve

    Greene County Parks preserve with ~6 miles of trails winding along the Little Miami National Scenic River, a 2.3-mile River Loop, a nature center, canoe/kayak launch, primitive camping and a raptor aviary. Free, open daily.

    Look for little miami river hike

    2575 Indian Ripple Rd, Beavercreek, OH 45385

    Recommended by Greene County Parks & Trails (official), Fairborn Daily Herald

  6. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Oakes Quarry Park

    Former limestone quarry, now Fairborn's second-largest park, exposing two of the oldest Silurian fossil coral reefs in the U.S. — one of the largest, most diverse Silurian-fauna sites in the world. Self-guided fossil trail; keep what you find in the spoil piles. Free, open daily.

    Look for silurian reef fossils

    1267 E Xenia Dr, Fairborn, OH 45324

    Recommended by City of Fairborn Parks & Recreation (official), Islands.com (travel editorial)

  7. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Downtown Fairborn Historic District

    Quirky, walkable Main Street at the gates of Wright-Patterson: Foy's — five nostalgic stores including a 1929 Halloween & variety shop — the macabre Secret Chamber house of oddities, indie boutiques, and a big third-weekend-of-October Halloween Festival with a Spooktacular Parade.

    Look for Foy's Halloween Main Street

    1 W Main St, Fairborn, OH 45324

    Recommended by Islands.com (travel editorial), City of Fairborn Parks & Recreation (official)

  8. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Wright State University Nutter Center

    The region's premier 11,200-seat arena (opened 1990) on the Wright State campus by Wright-Patterson: home of Raiders basketball and a regular tour stop for national touring concerts, comedians and family shows.

    Look for arena concerts basketball

    3640 Colonel Glenn Hwy, Fairborn, OH 45435

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  9. Worth the detour · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Wright Brothers Memorial

    17-foot pink-granite obelisk on Wright Brothers Hill (dedicated 1940 on Orville's birthday) with an overlook across Huffman Prairie and the Mad River valley. Free.

    2380 Memorial Rd, Wright-Patterson AFB, OH 45433

    Recommended by NATIONAL PARK SVC, NATIONAL PARK SVC

  10. Deep cut · Beavercreek, Fairborn & Wright-Patterson

    Caesar Creek Vineyards

    Family-owned, award-winning estate winery on 200 acres near the headwaters of Caesar Creek in Greene County; tasting room pours estate wines and cider with a vineyard view. A member of the Ohio Wine Producers Association.

    Look for estate winery tasting room

    962 Long Rd, Xenia, OH 45385

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Ohio Wine Producers Association, Dayton Local

Yellow Springs & Greene County 9

  1. Must see · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Glen Helen Nature Preserve

    1,000-acre preserve with 25 miles of trails, cascades and the iron-orange Yellow Spring that named the village; the day-trip centerpiece. $10 parking.

    405 Corry St, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  2. Must see · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    National Afro-American Museum & Cultural Center

    Ohio History Connection museum on the Wilberforce/Central State campuses documenting African American history and culture, from the Great Migration to civil-rights-era Ohio.

    1350 Brush Row Rd, Wilberforce, OH 45384

    Recommended by Ohio History Connection, Dayton Daily News / Dayton.com

  3. Must see · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Clifton Mill

    One of the largest water-powered grist mills still standing (built 1802) above the Little Miami gorge in Greene County; a working mill and restaurant, and host of a 4-million-light Christmas display.

    75 Water St, Clifton, OH 45316

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Dayton Local

  4. Must see · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Downtown Yellow Springs

    The funky, creative heart of the day trip: 75+ independent shops, galleries, pubs and eateries along Xenia Avenue — Dark Star Books, the Yellow Springs Toy Company, Village Artisans, the historic Little Art Theatre — plus Antioch College and the twice-yearly Street Fair (second Saturdays of June and October).

    Look for arts village shops street fair

    Xenia Ave, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Yellow Springs Ohio (destination guide), Islands.com (travel editorial)

  5. Must see · Ice Cream, Candy & Bakeries · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Young's Jersey Dairy

    Working dairy farm (Young family since 1869) just north of Yellow Springs: homemade ice cream, farmstead cheese, a petting barn, mini-golf and driving range — the classic day-trip stop.

    6880 Springfield-Xenia Rd, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Dayton Local

  6. Worth the detour · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Clifton Gorge State Nature Preserve

    Dramatic dolomite-and-limestone gorge cut by the Little Miami River, a National Natural Landmark with cliff-edge trails; adjoins John Bryan State Park.

    2381 OH-343, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Official site / operator, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

  7. Worth the detour · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    John Bryan State Park

    752-acre park called the most scenic in western Ohio, wrapping the Little Miami gorge with hiking, camping, rock climbing and a disc-golf course.

    3790 OH-370, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  8. Worth the detour · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Caesar Creek State Park

    Big reservoir park spanning Warren, Clinton and Greene counties — Ohio's premier fossil-hunting site, with a permit-and-palm-size rule letting visitors keep Ordovician brachiopods and corals from the designated zone, plus a 1,200-ft swimming beach, boating and miles of trails.

    Look for fossil hunting reservoir beach

    8570 OH-73, Waynesville, OH 45068

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

  9. Deep cut · Yellow Springs & Greene County

    Little Miami Scenic Trail

    Paved rail-trail on a National Scenic River corridor; the Yellow Springs Station (old depot, restrooms, parking) is a favorite trailhead for an easy bike ride into the village and gorge.

    101 Dayton St, Yellow Springs, OH 45387

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator

Springfield, Enon & Clark County 8

  1. Must see · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Frank Lloyd Wright's Westcott House

    Wright's only Prairie-style residence in Ohio (his first Ohio commission), designed 1906, built 1908, restored inch-by-inch in a $5.3M project reopened in 2005. On the National Register; hourly guided tours Tue-Sat 11-5, Sun 1-5. The marquee mid-corridor sight.

    1340 E High St, Springfield, OH 45505

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator, Frank Lloyd Wright Trust, Ohio.org (TourismOhio)

  2. Must see · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Hartman Rock Garden

    Depression-era folk-art masterpiece: unemployed molder Ben Hartman spent 1932-44 building a sprawling miniature world of hand-set stone and pebble monuments (Independence Hall, a castle, biblical and patriotic scenes) in his own yard. Preserved by the Kohler Foundation; free, open daily dawn-dusk. A nationally noted grassroots-art landmark.

    1905 Russell Ave, Springfield, OH 45506

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Kohler Foundation Inc., Visit Greater Springfield (Clark County CVB)

  3. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Enon Adena Mound (Knob Prairie Mound)

    Ohio's second-largest conical burial mound (after Miamisburg), about 40 ft high and 574 ft around, built by the Adena culture roughly 2,000 years ago and preserved on a residential circle in Enon. Owned by the village; free to view.

    Indian Dr at Mound Circle, Enon, OH 45323

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), The Historical Marker Database, Clio (heritage / history atlas), Enon Community Historical Society

  4. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Heritage Center of Clark County

    The Clark County Historical Society's museum in Springfield's grand 1890 Romanesque former City Hall and Market House. Local history from the Ice Age through Springfield's industrial heyday (Rogers greeting cards, farm machinery), plus a cafe under the rotunda.

    117 S Fountain Ave, Springfield, OH 45502

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Official site / operator, Ohio.org (TourismOhio)

  5. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Pennsylvania House Museum

    A Federal-style 1839 stagecoach tavern and inn built on the National Road, once a stopover for drovers and Conestoga-wagon pioneers. Saved from demolition by the DAR's Lagonda Chapter, run as a museum since 1941; on the National Register since 1973. Open limited days.

    1311 W Main St, Springfield, OH 45504

    Recommended by Wikipedia (published coordinates), Daughters of the American Revolution, The Historical Marker Database

  6. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    George Rogers Clark Park & Battle of Peckuwe Site

    Riverside park on the site of the 1780 Battle of Peckuwe, the largest Revolutionary War engagement west of the Alleghenies, where Col. George Rogers Clark's forces met the Shawnee. Trails, monuments to Clark and Tecumseh, and the Davidson Interpretive Center (across Lower Valley Pike).

    930 S Tecumseh Rd, Springfield, OH 45506

    Recommended by NTPRD, Springfield News-Sun, The Historical Marker Database

  7. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Madonna of the Trail

    The first of twelve identical DAR pioneer-mother monuments placed along the National Old Trails Road from Maryland to California, dedicated July 4, 1928 (Harry Truman attended). Springfield's was the first dedicated; moved in 2011 to National Road Commons downtown.

    W Main St at Fisher St (National Road Commons), Springfield, OH 45504

    Recommended by Ohio.org (TourismOhio), Daughters of the American Revolution, The Historical Marker Database

  8. Worth the detour · Springfield, Enon & Clark County

    Buck Creek State Park / C.J. Brown Reservoir

    1,900-acre ODNR park on the 2,120-acre C.J. Brown Reservoir just northeast of Springfield: swimming beach, marina, campground, cabins and trails, and a birding hotspot. From I-70 take Exit 59 north on SR-41.

    1976 Buck Creek Ln, Springfield, OH 45502

    Recommended by Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Wikipedia (published coordinates)

55 sights and 19 places to eat across Dayton and the Miami Valley, each traceable to the source that named it. The Gem City’s food story runs local — Marion’s Dayton-style pizza, Esther Price candy, Bill’s Donuts, the Pine Club and the Oregon District — but the real draw is aviation: the National Museum of the U.S. Air Force (the world’s largest, free) and the Wright brothers’ workshops.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Dayton’s signature strength is aviation and hometown classics: the National Museum of the U.S. Air Force (the world’s largest, free), the Wright brothers’ Carillon Flyer III, Marion’s Dayton-style pizza, Esther Price candy and Bill’s Donuts, sourced to the Dayton Daily News, Dayton Magazine, WHIO and the National Park Service. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation, SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open.
